intro: Every box is one kind of record the app keeps. Start with a group, then click a table to see what it is for, what it belongs to, and what happens around it. Hover any line to read the connection in plain words.

auth.users.label: Login accounts
auth.users.what: One row per login account (email and password) that the sign-in system keeps. Everyone who signs in has one: staff, and dealership contacts using the client portal. The rest of the app links its own people records back to this account.
auth.users.who: the system automatically, created by admins when they add staff or when a dealership contact signs up for the portal

users.label: Staff profiles
users.what: One row per member of your own staff: name, employee number, role, pay rate, home location, manager, hire date and similar details. Created by an admin through the Create User screen at the same moment the login account is made.
users.who: admins and finance create them; managers, finance and admins read them

users_safe_view.label: Safe staff list
users_safe_view.what: Not a real table: a trimmed-down, read-only copy of the staff profiles that leaves out sensitive fields like pay rate, date of birth and emergency contacts. Screens that only need to look up a name, such as the staff search box and the payroll dashboard, read this instead of the full profile.
users_safe_view.who: the system automatically; used by anyone allowed to search for a staff member

user_roles.label: Staff role grants
user_roles.what: One row per role a login account has been granted: employee, manager, finance, admin or super admin. This is the record the app actually checks to decide what someone may see and do. Written when the account is created and whenever an admin changes someone's role.

user_locations.label: Staff location assignments
user_locations.what: One row per staff member paired with a location they are allowed to work at and see. Set by an admin when creating or editing a user, and also filled in automatically: adding a new location gives every admin access to it, and granting someone the admin role gives them every existing location.

locations.label: Service locations
locations.what: One row per physical site where work is done, such as a dealership lot or a yard. Each location belongs to one client company and carries its name, address and map coordinates. Added by an admin, or created when an approved dealership location request is processed.

clients.label: Client companies
clients.what: One row per customer company you bill: name, business type (for example dealership), billing contact, tax details and payment terms. Created by an admin through the client screens or the client setup wizard.

work_types.label: Kinds of service
work_types.what: One row per kind of work you sell, such as a standard wash, a detail or an hourly service. It is the shared list every price and every logged job is built on, so it changes rarely.

rate_configs.label: Price list entries
rate_configs.what: One row per agreed price: this client, at this location, for this kind of service, at this rate and frequency. It is the rate card behind billing, and can be flagged as needing a price review. Set up by finance or admins on the rate card screen.

work_items.label: Vehicles and units
work_items.what: One row per individual thing that gets serviced, usually a vehicle, identified by its number or plate and attached to one price list entry. Added by staff on the work items screen, by the add-vehicle popup, or in bulk from a spreadsheet import.

work_logs.label: Completed work
work_logs.what: One row per piece of work an employee actually did: which vehicle or service, what date, how many, and any notes. This is the core billing record. Created by the employee on their weekly dashboard as they log washes.
work_logs.who: employees, with managers, finance and admins reviewing and correcting

wash_requests.label: Wash requests
wash_requests.what: One row per vehicle a dealership contact asked to have washed in a given week, at one of their locations. Created from the client portal; it is marked as done automatically as soon as an employee logs matching work for that vehicle.
wash_requests.who: dealership portal users create them; employees see them as starred vehicles

employee_comments.label: Messages
employee_comments.what: One row per message posted about a week's work at a location: a note between a manager and an employee, or an automatic note announcing that a dealership requested or cancelled washes. Can be addressed to one person or left open to the location's team.
employee_comments.who: employees, managers, admins and dealership portal users

message_replies.label: Message replies
message_replies.what: One row per reply written under a message. Keeps the back-and-forth of a conversation in order.
message_replies.who: employees, managers, admins and dealership portal users

message_reads.label: Message read marks
message_reads.what: One row saying a particular person has read a particular message. It is what makes the unread badge go away.
message_reads.who: the system automatically, when someone opens a message

user_message_views.label: Message inbox check-ins
user_message_views.what: One row per person recording the last time they looked at their messages. Used to count how many messages arrived since then.

tickets.label: Job tickets
tickets.what: One row per ticket raised about a specific job or problem at a location, with an automatic ticket number like TKT-000123, an optional photo, and a status of open, in progress or closed. Submitted from the ticket popup by staff.
tickets.who: employees and managers raise them; admins and finance answer and close them

ticket_line_items.label: Ticket detail lines
ticket_line_items.what: One row per numbered line of detail on a ticket, so a single ticket can list several items or issues in order. Entered at the same time the ticket is submitted.

ticket_replies.label: Ticket replies
ticket_replies.what: One row per reply added to a ticket conversation, with who wrote it and when.
ticket_replies.who: the person who raised the ticket and the admins or finance staff answering it

ticket_views.label: Ticket check-ins
ticket_views.what: One row per person recording the last time they looked at the ticket list, so the app can show how many tickets have arrived or changed since then.

error_reports.label: Problem reports
error_reports.what: One row per problem someone reported from inside the app using the report button, including the page they were on, an optional screenshot, and the browser they used. An admin can write a response and mark it handled.
error_reports.who: any signed-in person reports them; super admins respond

error_report_replies.label: Problem report replies
error_report_replies.what: One row per reply in the conversation about a reported problem, between the person who reported it and an admin.

client_portal_users.label: Portal accounts
client_portal_users.what: One row per dealership contact who uses the client portal: their name, company, email, whether they are approved, and when they last signed in. Created when the contact first signs in and is confirmed, or set up directly by an admin.
client_portal_users.who: dealership portal users and the admins who approve them

client_portal_access_requests.label: Portal access requests
client_portal_access_requests.what: One row per location a portal contact has asked to be given access to, with an optional note, plus the decision and reviewer once it is handled. Created from the portal's request-access screen.
client_portal_access_requests.who: dealership portal users create them; admins and finance review them

client_portal_location_access.label: Portal location access
client_portal_location_access.what: One row per portal contact paired with a location they are allowed to see. Added automatically the moment an admin approves their access request, and removed if their account is later denied or deleted.
client_portal_location_access.who: the system automatically, on an admin's approval

dealership_location_requests.label: New location requests
dealership_location_requests.what: One row per request from the field asking for a new dealership site to be set up, with the proposed company and location name and address. A reviewer either rejects it, merges it into an existing client, or approves it, which creates the client and location records.
dealership_location_requests.who: employees and managers request; admins and finance review

dealership_rates.label: Dealership per-vehicle rates
dealership_rates.what: One row per agreed per-vehicle price for a dealership client, optionally narrowed to one of its locations, with the date it takes effect. Appears to be the newer, simpler pricing used for high-volume dealership work alongside the main price list.

dealership_wash_batches.label: Dealership daily counts
dealership_wash_batches.what: One row per employee, per dealership location, per day, holding just a vehicle count, the rate used and optional notes. It is the fast way to record bulk dealership work without listing every vehicle; re-saving the same day updates the same row.
dealership_wash_batches.who: employees at dealership locations; finance reads it for reporting

payroll_periods.label: Pay periods
payroll_periods.what: One row per pay period, with its start and end dates, the check date, and whether it is still a draft or has been locked. Created by finance on the payroll dashboard before a payroll run.

payroll_pay_codes.label: Pay codes
payroll_pay_codes.what: One row per pay code your payroll provider recognises, grouped by department, with its default pay type. It is the shared reference list the rest of payroll points at.

payroll_employee_lines.label: Standing pay setup
payroll_employee_lines.what: One row per recurring pay line for a person: their display name, department, task label, pay code, pay type and rate, with the dates it applies. It is the template that each payroll run starts from.

payroll_hours_imports.label: Imported hours
payroll_hours_imports.what: One row per line of hours brought in from an outside timekeeping file for a pay period, including regular and overtime hours and the raw name as it appeared in the file. Loaded by finance uploading the file on the payroll dashboard; reloading replaces the whole period's import.

payroll_run_lines.label: Payroll run lines
payroll_run_lines.what: One row per line that will actually be paid in a period: person, pay code, task, quantity or hours, overtime and rate. Built automatically when finance generates the run by combining logged work, imported hours and the standing pay setup, then edited by hand as needed.
payroll_run_lines.who: finance, with the system building the first draft automatically

payroll_work_type_map.label: Work-to-pay translation
payroll_work_type_map.what: One row saying that a given kind of service, optionally at a specific location, should be paid under a given pay code and task label. It is the lookup that turns completed work into payroll lines.

system_settings.label: System settings
system_settings.what: One row per adjustable setting, such as the weekly entry cutoff date, stored as a name and a value with a short description. Changed by admins on the settings screen, and the cutoff can also roll forward on its own.
system_settings.who: admins and super admins; some values are read by everyone

system_settings_audit.label: Settings change history
system_settings_audit.what: One row per change to a setting, recording the old value, the new value, who changed it and why. Written automatically whenever a setting is updated, so nothing can be changed without a trace.

audit_log.label: Record change history
audit_log.what: One row per tracked change to a work or wash record, keeping a before-and-after copy plus who made the change. Written automatically in the background rather than by anyone using a screen.
audit_log.who: the system automatically; managers and admins can read it

activity_logs.label: Usage trail
activity_logs.what: One row per notable thing someone did in the app: the page they were on, the action, and the target. Recorded automatically as people click around, and older entries can be cleared out on a retention schedule.
activity_logs.who: the system automatically; only super admins can read it

manager_approval_requests.label: Manager approval requests
manager_approval_requests.what: One row per request for a manager to approve a change to a specific wash entry, with a reason and a decision. No current screen reads or writes it, so it appears to be an earlier approval feature that is no longer in active use.
manager_approval_requests.who: appears to be unused; originally employees requesting and managers deciding

report_templates.label: Saved report setups
report_templates.what: One row per saved reporting setup: its name, the filters it applies, whether it is shared with others, and how often it has been used. Saved by finance or admins from the report screens so a favourite report can be re-run.

locations.label: Sites and who works there
locations.what: The physical sites you service and the list of which staff members are assigned to each one.

users.label: Staff and system records
users.what: Staff profiles plus the app-wide housekeeping records: settings, their change history, the usage trail and the read markers behind unread badges.

auth.users.label: Login accounts and permissions
auth.users.what: The sign-in accounts themselves and the things hung directly off them: role grants, saved report setups and the older manager approval requests.

client_portal_users.label: Portal, work and pricing
client_portal_users.what: The dealership-facing portal accounts and access, together with the day-to-day operating records they touch: services, prices, vehicles, wash requests and completed work.

clients.label: Client companies
clients.what: The customer companies you bill, their dealership rates, their bulk daily wash counts and requests to open new sites for them.

payroll_employee_lines.label: Payroll
payroll_employee_lines.what: Everything needed to run a pay period: the periods themselves, imported hours, each person's standing pay setup and the final lines to be paid.

employee_comments.label: Messages
employee_comments.what: Week-by-week conversations between managers, employees and dealership contacts, with their replies and read markers.

tickets.label: Job tickets
tickets.what: Numbered tickets raised about specific jobs or problems at a location, with their detail lines and reply threads.

error_reports.label: Problem reports
error_reports.what: Problems people report from inside the app, and the replies between the reporter and an admin.

standalone.label: Not connected to anything
standalone.what: Tables that stand on their own with no links to the rest.

flows.title: An employee logs work for the week

steps.text: The employee opens their weekly dashboard. It shows only the locations they are assigned to, and for the location they pick it lists the vehicles and services that have an active price set up.
They add each vehicle they washed on the right day. Every entry becomes one completed-work record holding the date, the quantity, the vehicle, the price it is linked to and the employee's own name.

The moment that record is saved, the system checks for any open wash request for the same vehicle in that week or earlier and marks it fulfilled, pointing it at the work that satisfied it. Nobody has to close requests by hand.
If the day falls before the current entry cutoff, the dashboard shows it as closed and blocks the entry. Finance and admins can still enter it, and it is flagged as an override.
In the background the app records the change history of the work record and a usage-trail entry, so corrections can be traced later.

flows.title: A dealership asks for washes through the portal

steps.text: An approved dealership contact signs in to the portal and picks one of the locations they have been given access to.
The portal shows the active vehicles and services at that location, already marking any that have been requested this week so nothing gets asked for twice.
They tick the vehicles they want washed and submit. One wash request record is created per vehicle for the current week; asking again for the same vehicle in the same week is quietly ignored.
A message is posted to that location listing exactly what was requested plus any note, so the crew sees it. Requested vehicles show a gold star on the employee dashboard until they are washed.
If they change their mind, the contact can remove a request that has not yet been fulfilled, and a cancellation message is posted to the same location.

flows.title: A new staff member gets an account

steps.text: An admin fills in the Create User screen. Before anything is saved, the app confirms the person doing this is an admin or higher and is not trying to grant a role above their own.

A login account is created with a temporary password, then a staff profile is saved with the same identity, holding the employee number, name, home location, manager and role, and flagged so the person must change their password at first sign-in.
A role grant record is added. If that role is admin or super admin, the system immediately assigns them to every existing location, so they can see the whole business without anyone ticking boxes.
For a regular employee or manager, the admin instead picks the specific locations, and one assignment record is saved per location.
A welcome email with sign-in instructions is sent. If the email fails, the account is still created and the admin is told the email did not go out.

flows.title: A dealership contact gets portal access

steps.text: The contact signs in to the portal for the first time. The app checks their email is not already a staff account, then creates a portal account marked as pending approval.
They complete a short onboarding form with their name, company and work location, which fills in their portal account details.
They pick the locations they need to see and submit one access request per location, with an optional note explaining who they are.

An admin or finance user reviews the pending requests. Approving one immediately grants that portal account access to that location and stamps the request with the decision, the reviewer and the time.
An admin can separately mark the whole portal account approved or denied. Denying it also strips away every location the account had been given.
Finance opens the payroll dashboard and creates the pay period by entering its start and end dates, then sets the check date. It starts as a draft.
They upload the hours file from the outside timekeeping system. Each line becomes an imported-hours record for that period; re-uploading clears the period's previous import first.
Each person's standing pay setup, meaning their department, task, pay code, pay type and rate, is kept on the same screen and is what the run is built from.

They generate the run. The app pulls all completed work inside the period, translates each kind of service into the right pay code and task using the work-to-pay lookup, folds in the imported hours, and writes the resulting payroll lines, replacing any earlier draft for that period.
Finance edits individual lines where needed, then locks the period. Locking stamps the time and stops further changes.

flows.title: A ticket is raised and answered

steps.text: A staff member opens the submit-ticket popup, picks the client and location, describes the job and can attach a photo. Saving creates a ticket with an automatic number like TKT-000123, opened as new.
Any extra detail lines typed on the form are saved as numbered lines under that ticket, keeping the order they were entered in.
Admins and finance see the ticket in the list and write replies. Each reply is its own record with the author and time, so the thread stays readable.
Whoever is handling it moves the status from open to in progress and finally to closed. The last-changed time is stamped automatically on every update.
Each person's last look at the ticket list is remembered, which is how the unread ticket badge is counted.

flows.title: A new location is set up

steps.text: Someone in the field submits a request for a new dealership site, proposing a company name, a location name and an address.

A reviewer opens it and is shown existing client companies with similar names, so they can merge it into one that already exists rather than create a duplicate. They can also simply reject it with notes.
On approval, a client company is created if it is genuinely new, then the location is created under the chosen client, and the request is stamped with the decision and linked to what it produced.
As soon as the location exists, every admin and super admin is automatically assigned to it, so nobody has to remember to grant that access.
The person who asked for the site is assigned to it too, and finance then adds the price list entries and vehicles that make the location usable for logging work.
The cutoff date is stored as a single named setting. It is the earliest date employees are still allowed to enter work for, normally the previous Saturday night.
It can roll forward on its own to the new Saturday, and an admin can also extend it by a week or reset it from the settings screen.
Whichever way it changes, the change is recorded automatically with the old value, the new value, who changed it and the reason. That history cannot be skipped.
From that moment, the employee dashboard shows closed days as locked and refuses new entries for them. Finance and admins can still enter work for closed days, marked as an override.

terms.client: A customer company you bill, such as a dealership group or a fleet operator.
terms.location: A single physical site where work is done. Each one belongs to one client company.
terms.work type: A kind of service you sell, such as a standard wash, a detail, or an hourly service.
terms.work item: One individual thing that gets serviced, almost always a specific vehicle identified by its number.
terms.rate config / price list entry: The agreed price for one kind of service, for one client, at one location.
terms.work log: The record of work an employee actually completed on a given day. This is what billing and payroll are built from.
terms.wash request: A dealership contact asking through the portal for a specific vehicle to be washed in a given week.
terms.fulfilled: A wash request that has been matched to real completed work, so it no longer needs doing.
terms.client portal: The separate, limited part of the app that dealership contacts sign in to. They can see their own locations, request washes, view history and exchange messages, and nothing else.
terms.portal account: A dealership contact's profile in the portal, kept apart from your staff records. It has to be approved before it is useful.
terms.cutoff date: The earliest date employees may still enter work for. It normally closes each Saturday night; finance and admins can enter work past it.
terms.override entry: Work entered for a day that is already past the cutoff. Only finance and admins can do it, and it is flagged as such.
terms.dealership batch: A shortcut for high-volume dealership sites: one daily total number of vehicles and the rate used, instead of listing each vehicle.
terms.pay period: The stretch of dates one payroll run covers, with a check date. Locking it freezes the numbers.
terms.pay code: The code your payroll provider uses to classify a line of pay. Each kind of service is translated into one before payroll is produced.
terms.payroll run line: A single line that will actually be paid: one person, one pay code, a quantity or hours, and a rate.
terms.ticket: A numbered record raised about a specific job or problem at a location, worked to a close through replies and a status.
terms.message: A note attached to one location and one week, used between managers, employees and dealership contacts. The portal also posts them automatically for wash requests.
terms.role: What someone is allowed to do: employee, manager, finance, admin or super admin. Higher roles can do everything the lower ones can.
terms.super admin: The highest level of access, including the usage trail and the raw database screens.
terms.location assignment: The link that says a staff member may work at and see a particular location. Admins get every location automatically.
terms.audit trail: An automatic before-and-after record of a change, kept so you can always see what was altered, by whom and when.
terms.table: One kind of record the app keeps, like a spreadsheet tab: one row per thing, one column per fact about it.
terms.access rule: A rule stored with a table that says which kinds of users may see or change its rows. The app relies on these for privacy between staff, finance and dealership contacts.
terms.automatic action: Something the database does on its own when a record is added or changed, without a screen being involved: writing history, closing a wash request, assigning locations to a new admin.
